blocking.issue: The new TM-4 sentence offers 'commit them' as a way out, and the code then silently drops the person's commit. If the person commits the folder's change as the row tells them, the next poll's rebuild resets the task branch to the host's (`git.createBranch(branch, origin/${branch})` right after the dirty check). The commit ends up on no branch, is never pushed, and the file is gone from the folder; only the reflog keeps it. Nothing tells the person. This breaks design §5 rule 9 (no promises the code does not keep) and rule 8 (the 'what to do' must work) for a new person-facing sentence.

Update the user guide paragraph and ADR 0111 point 5 to match, and name the new wording in notes_for_other_areas for polish-words.

blocking.issue: A sibling of TM-1 is missed (validation rule 8): an empty pull request is still offered for Merge. `holdsOwnChange` runs before the sync. When main already holds the task's change, a run that resumes the open pull request's branch (Tasks tab Redo, or a rework run) passes the check. The rebase onto main then drops the already-upstream commit, the branch becomes main's head, and it is force-pushed (`force: !!existingPr`). The critic accepts and the Overview offers Merge on a pull request with no change. This is the same visible failure as the [major] TM-1, and the report neither fixes nor logs it.
blocking.evidence: Bench steps 26-30 (/tmp/frbench/review-leftovers7-tailmerge/steps/29-tm1c-overview-after.png). main had the same footer.html as PR #3 (diff empty). I pressed Redo on the Tasks tab, then Start. After the session the task was done, 'Accepted · waiting for you to merge'. PR #3's head was 6940bae, equal to main (`git diff main <branch>` empty), and GET /repos/bench/seeded/pulls/3/files returned []. The Overview listed #3 with Merge. The code has behaved this way since before the branch; the fix's check is placed before the rebase, so it does not cover this case.
blocking.expected: Read the task's own change again after the sync (rebase or merge) and before the push: for example, `changedFiles` already computed at :975 is empty, or `holdsOwnChange` is false after `synced`. An existing pull request then takes the TM-1 path (close it with one sentence, or fail as a no-change task) instead of being force-pushed to the base's head. Add a composed test: an open pull request whose change has landed on main, Redo from the Tasks tab, and assert that no empty pull request is offered for Merge. Alternatively, log it as a new U-entry with the evidence if the session lead defers it.

docs/user-guide.md:350 says 'once they are put away, the rebuild runs at the next check and your Merge goes on'. When the owed rebuild drops a closed dependency (rebuilt_without), the Merge does not go on: the record waits for the person again with the warning (bench step 14). Say that the row then says what came of the rebuild.
Before Merge is pressed, a row whose rebuild is owed and whose folder holds changes shows a plain Merge with no hint (bench step 06; fixer's step 06 too). The wait is said only after the click.
TM-4's sentence names 'its task's folder' without saying where it is or offering Open folder. A person cannot easily act on it (polish-words / polish-screens).

Critic column shows a raw lowercase verdict, 'accepted', for a failed task and for a 'Mark done anyway' task (bench steps 41, 46). This existed before this branch (taskCheck returns null when the task is not done) and breaks design §2/§5 plain words; for polish.

emptiedSentence 'Redone from main, it changed nothing, so #4 was closed.' is a comma splice. The no-change fallback '<summary>\n(no changes were made in the worktree)', which existed before, is still what a Try again on the same task shows. Both are polish-words' to reword.

The bench stand-in writes different content on a redo (the 'quotes' switch), so TM-1 could be walked only by giving main the redo's own output and pressing Redo within one poll. Reaching it took three attempts (steps 31-44).

finishUnfinished: (a) a resolved file that legitimately has a line starting with '<<<<<<< ' or '>>>>>>> ' is read as unresolved forever; (b) unstaged edits to other files during the person's rebase make `rebase --continue` refuse, and must() throws, so the run fails with git's text. Both are edge cases and untested.
